articles.title: Ceylan Worldwide: Sri Lanka’s Largest Promotional Apparel Enterprise with Triple ISO Certification
articles.text:
Ceylan Worldwide (Pvt) Ltd has achieved Triple ISO Certification , comprising ISO 9001 (Quality Management), ISO 14001 (Environmental Management), and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety). This milestone positions Ceylan as Sri Lanka’s largest promotional apparel enterprise to hold all three certifications, underscoring its leadership in responsible excellence.
Founded in 2009, Ceylan Worldwide has grown from a pioneering Sri Lankan enterprise into a trusted international partner in premium corporate apparel and customized promotional merchandise. Over the years, the company has built a reputation for excellence, serving a customer base of more than 1,000 organizations worldwide . Guided by innovation, ethical practices, and customercentric values, its operations span marketing, manufacturing, branding execution, and distribution — all supported by a robust Integrated Management System (IMS) Policy.
As a participant of the United Nations Global Compact, Ceylan aligns its strategies with universal principles relating to human rights, labor, environment, and anticorruption. The Triple ISO Certification further reinforces this commitment, ensuring that every product and process contributes positively to people and the community.
Krishan Kollure, Director, said: “Our Triple ISO Certification is a reflection of the discipline and precision in our production processes. From raw material sourcing to final delivery, every stage is managed with strict quality controls, environmental responsibility, and safety standards. This achievement proves that our factory operations are aligned with international benchmarks, ensuring reliability and consistency across every customer order and delivering products that meet our quality standards.”
Sonali Hewage, Director – Corporate Communications & Compliance, said: “Leading this certification journey was both a responsibility and a privilege. Achieving ISO 9001, ISO 14001, and ISO 45001 is a proud achievement that reflects our team’s dedication to quality, sustainability, and workplace safety. With over 15 years of experience, these certifications reinforce the strength of our IMS Policy and our commitment to ensuring product quality, reducing environmental impact, and safeguarding both staff and clients.”
articles.summary: Ceylan Worldwide (Pvt) Ltd has achieved Triple ISO Certification , comprising ISO 9001 (Quality Management), ISO 14001 (Environmental Management), and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety). This milestone positions Ceylan as Sri Lanka’s largest promotional apparel enterprise to hold all three certifications, underscoring its leadership in responsible excellence.

articles.title: Suresh Sallay produced before court in Prageeth Ekneligoda disappearance case
articles.text:
Former State Intelligence Chief Suresh Sallay, who is currently in the custody of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), was produced before the Permanent Three-Judge High Court-at-Bar today (16) to provide evidence in the case concerning the disappearance of journalist Prageeth Ekneligoda.
According to reports, Sallay was brought before the court when the case was taken up for hearing today.
The case relates to the disappearance of Prageeth Ekneligoda, a journalist attached to the Lanka eNews website, who went missing on January 24, 2010, just two days before Sri Lanka’s presidential election.
Ekneligoda disappeared shortly after publishing articles supporting the opposition presidential candidate at the time.
His disappearance remains one of Sri Lanka’s most prominent unresolved cases involving a journalist.
articles.summary: Former State Intelligence Chief Suresh Sallay, who is currently in the custody of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), was produced before the Permanent Three-Judge High Court-at-Bar today (16) to provide evidence in the case concerning the disappearance of journalist Prageeth Ekneligoda.

articles.title: Wildlife vets working around the clock to save Kawanthissa elephant – Ministry
articles.text:
The Ministry of Environment has urged the public to avoid gathering near the location where Kawanthissa the elephant, who remains in critical condition, is receiving treatment.
In a statement, the Ministry said specialist veterinary teams from the Department of Wildlife Conservation are working around the clock to save the elephant, administering saline and essential medications while carrying out necessary medical procedures to stabilize his condition.
However, the Ministry warned that large gatherings near the treatment area could cause severe stress to the elephant and disrupt the sensitive medical procedures being carried out by veterinary teams.
According to wildlife veterinarians, maintaining a quiet and calm environment is essential to help stabilize the elephant’s heart rate, blood pressure and physical responses.
The Ministry has therefore requested the public to refrain from entering the treatment area unnecessarily, gathering near the location, making excessive noise or operating drone cameras.
It also urged the public to allow veterinary teams to carry out their duties without interference.
The Ministry emphasised that the best way for the public to show their concern and compassion for Kawanthissa is to maintain a peaceful environment and support the veterinary teams working to save his life.

articles.title: Gnanasara Thera protest: Monks move out of Presidential Secretariat
articles.text:
The protest by a group of Buddhist monks outside the Presidential Secretariat in Colombo, demanding the release of Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, has ended.
According to reports, the monks have removed the temporary shelters erected at the protest site in compliance with a court order issued today (16), and moved away from the site.
The move follows an order issued by Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena this morning, prohibiting Ven. Ulapane Sumangala Thera and 54 others from remaining within the premises of the Presidential Secretariat.
The protesting monks reportedly removed the temporary structures in respect of the court order.
The protest began on Thursday (15) evening, with a group of Buddhist monks gathering outside the Presidential Secretariat to demand the release of the imprisoned Gnanasara Thera.
Several monks remained at the location overnight, continuing their protest into Friday (16).
The protesters had been occupying the pavement on the opposite side of Galle Road, away from the Presidential Secretariat.
The removal of the temporary shelters followed the court’s intervention as the monks continued their demonstration demanding Gnanasara Thera’s release.

articles.title: US announces $17 Mn investment to digitize Colombo Port operations
articles.text:
The United States today (16) announced a US$ 17 million investment to digitize operations at the Port of Colombo, aimed at strengthening one of South Asia’s busiest and most strategically important maritime trade hubs.
According to a statement issued by the US Embassy in Sri Lanka, the project will be implemented in partnership with the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA), introducing new digital systems using American technology to streamline port operations, accelerate cargo movement and reduce shipping delays and costs.
The US-funded project will support the development of two interconnected digital systems, the Maritime Single Window and the Port Community System, to improve coordination and accelerate cargo processing at the Port of Colombo.
These systems will enable shipping companies, Customs officials, immigration authorities, port operators and businesses to exchange information electronically, reducing paperwork and delays caused by disconnected procedures.
The Embassy stated that the Port of Colombo handles an estimated US$ 30 billion in US-related cargo annually, serving as a major transshipment hub connecting South Asia with global markets.
US Ambassador to Sri Lanka Eric Meyer said more than 500,000 containers carrying US inbound and outbound cargo pass through the Port of Colombo each year, representing billions of dollars in trade.
He noted that improving port efficiency and reducing shipping costs would strengthen supply chains, benefit American businesses and consumers, and create new commercial opportunities for American technology companies.
Meanwhile, Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation Anura Karunathilaka said modernizing port operations is essential to maintaining Colombo’s position as a regional maritime hub.
He stated that the project would improve trade facilitation, attract business and strengthen Sri Lanka’s connections to international markets.
SLPA Chairman Dr. Parakrama Dissanayake also welcomed the initiative, stating that the new digital systems would improve coordination among agencies and businesses involved in port operations while providing more efficient and predictable services to shipping lines and customers.
According to the US Embassy, the project will also create opportunities for American technology companies to provide the hardware, software and technical expertise required for the digital upgrade.
An open and competitive selection process will be conducted to appoint an implementing partner.
The Embassy further stated that the investment is expected to strengthen critical international trade routes, support US supply chains and reinforce Sri Lanka’s role as a key maritime trading partner in the Indian Ocean.
articles.summary: The United States today (16) announced a US$ 17 million investment to digitize operations at the Port of Colombo, aimed at strengthening one of South Asia’s busiest and most strategically important maritime trade hubs.

articles.title: Sri Lanka to strengthen Global Tourism Promotion with World Bank support
articles.text:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Tourism has taken steps to advance Sri Lanka’s Global Destination Marketing and Communication Campaign, aimed at strengthening the country’s position as a competitive and attractive international tourism destination.
According to a statement issued by Sri Lanka Tourism, a high-level discussion on the implementation of the campaign, supported by the World Bank, was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism.
The meeting focused on adopting a long-term, data-driven approach to tourism promotion, based on an analysis of tourism demand and supply trends, visitor behaviour, destination branding and international marketing strategies.
Discussions also highlighted the importance of ensuring a transparent procurement process and strengthening institutional capacity for the successful implementation and long-term sustainability of the campaign.
The initiative will receive technical expertise and strategic guidance from MTI Consulting and Skift Inc./JD to develop and implement a globally competitive destination marketing programme.
The campaign is expected to strengthen collaboration between public and private sector stakeholders while establishing a sustainable roadmap for promoting Sri Lanka in key international tourism markets.
According to the Ministry, the initiative is expected to increase tourist arrivals, generate economic opportunities and contribute to the country’s broader economic growth.
The discussion was attended by Secretary to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism Aruni Ranaraja, heads of tourism institutions under the Ministry, representatives of SLAITO, TAASL, the Tourism Advisory Committee, the World Bank, MTI Consulting and Skift Inc./JD, and Director General of National Planning H.P. Somathilaka.
articles.summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Tourism has taken steps to advance Sri Lanka’s Global Destination Marketing and Communication Campaign, aimed at strengthening the country’s position as a competitive and attractive international tourism destination.

articles.title: Gnanasara Thera’s imprisonment discussed as Prison Officials meet Mahanayake Theras
articles.text:
A group of senior prison officials, including Commissioner of Prisons (Operations and Media) Senaka Palletenna, met with the Mahanayake Theras of the Asgiri and Malwathu Chapters in Kandy today (16).
During the meeting at the Asgiri Maha Viharaya, the Mahanayake of the Asgiri Chapter, Most Ven. Warakagoda Sri Gnanarathana Thera, called for the release of imprisoned Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera.
The Mahanayake Thera inquired whether there was a procedure through which Gnanasara Thera could be granted release.
Responding to the question, Commissioner of Prisons Senaka Palletanna stated that no definite decision had been taken regarding the matter so far.
Following the meeting, the Commissioner of Prisons visited the Malwathu Maha Viharaya, where he met the Mahanayake of the Malwathu Chapter, Most Ven. Thibbatuwawe Sri Sumangala Thera.
During the discussion, the Malwathu Mahanayake Thera emphasised the need to establish separate detention facilities for Buddhist monks who are remanded or imprisoned over criminal charges.
He noted that although discussions had previously been held on the matter, they had concluded without reaching a decision.
The Mahanayake Thera further stressed that Buddhist monks held in custody should be accommodated in a separate facility where they are permitted to engage in religious activities without restrictions.
He also emphasised the importance of ensuring that imprisoned Buddhist monks are treated appropriately and with dignity.

articles.title: Severe lightning advisory issued for several parts of Sri Lanka
articles.text:
The Department of Meteorology has issued an advisory for severe lightning in five provinces and five districts, valid until 11.30 p.m. today (16).
According to the advisory, thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely to occur at several places in the Sabaragamuwa, Central, North-Central, Uva and North-Western provinces, as well as the Batticaloa, Trincomalee, Mullaitivu, Vavuniya and Mannar districts.
The Met Department also warned that temporary localized strong winds may occur during thundershowers.
The public has been advised to take adequate precautions to minimize damage caused by lightning activity.
People are urged to seek shelter indoors, avoid open areas such as paddy fields and open water bodies, and refrain from using wired telephones and connected electrical appliances during thunderstorms.
The Department also advised the public to avoid travelling in open vehicles, including bicycles, tractors and boats, and to remain cautious of fallen trees and power lines.
In case of emergencies, the public is requested to contact local disaster management authorities.

articles.title: Yan Oya’s first cage fish farming project generates nearly Rs. 700,000 in revenue
articles.text:
The first cage fish farming project at the Yan Oya Reservoir has recorded a successful harvest, generating an income of nearly Rs. 700,000, according to the National Aquaculture Development Authority (NAQDA).
The pilot project, implemented by NAQDA, recorded its first harvest on Thursday (15), producing a total of 1,202 kilograms of fish from 2,996 fish, with a reported income of Rs. 696,000.
The fish were sold at a rate of Rs. 600 per kilogram, with the Ceylon Fisheries Corporation purchasing 500 kilograms and a private fish trader in the area purchasing another 660 kilograms.
Under the project, the rearing of 15,000 fish fingerlings commenced on May 18, 2026. Subsequently, 3,600 advanced fingerlings weighing over 50 grams each were introduced into a circular cage on July 30.
According to NAQDA, this marks the first time a circular cage has been used in Sri Lanka for the commercial-scale production of fish for human consumption.
The initiative was introduced as part of efforts to address the country’s annual fish shortage, which requires an additional 300,000 metric tonnes of fish, while also strengthening the rural economy.
NAQDA Chairman Kithsiri Dharmapriya, along with officials and members of the Yan Oya fishing community, participated in the harvesting event.

articles.title: Sri Lanka seeks EU investments under €300 Bn Global Gateway Initiative
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has sought European Union (EU) investments to strengthen its small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), startup ecosystem and export-oriented industries under the EU’s Global Gateway investment initiative.
The proposal was discussed during a meeting held on Thursday (15) between Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Chathuranga Abeysinghe and visiting European Commission official Pēteris Ustubs, Director for Asia, Central Asia and the Pacific at the Directorate-General for International Partnerships (DG INTPA).
The EU’s Global Gateway initiative aims to mobilise nearly €300 billion in global investments across key sectors, including digital technology, renewable energy, transport infrastructure, healthcare, education and research.
During the discussion, Deputy Minister Abeysinghe highlighted the need to upgrade Sri Lanka’s SME sector to meet international trade standards and strengthen its access to export markets.
He also emphasised the importance of establishing startup incubators to support emerging entrepreneurs in transforming business ideas into commercially viable ventures.
Accordingly, the Deputy Minister sought EU investments in capital and technology to support local SMEs and establish startup incubators, with the aim of developing Sri Lanka’s export-oriented industries.
He further invited European investors to consider Sri Lanka as a strategic gateway to Asian markets, citing its location along major international maritime routes, skilled workforce and ongoing governance reforms.
The Deputy Minister also briefed the EU delegation on economic reforms being implemented under Sri Lanka’s International Monetary Fund (IMF) Extended Fund Facility programme.
Meanwhile, EU official Pēteris Ustubs welcomed Sri Lanka’s progress under the IMF programme, particularly the successful completion of its fifth and sixth reviews, stating that these developments send a positive signal to international investors regarding the country’s economic direction.
The discussions also focused on strengthening regional energy connectivity in South Asia, promoting renewable energy projects and advancing transparent infrastructure development.
Deputy Minister Abeysinghe reiterated the government’s commitment to modernising Sri Lanka’s industrial and business sectors while ensuring transparency in attracting foreign investments.
The meeting was also attended by Deputy Head of the EU Delegation in Colombo Galia Agiševa and Head of Cooperation at the EU Delegation Virginie Lafleur-Tighe.
articles.summary: Sri Lanka has sought European Union (EU) investments to strengthen its small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), startup ecosystem and export-oriented industries under the EU’s Global Gateway investment initiative. The EU’s Global Gateway initiative aims to mobilise nearly €300 billion in global investments across key sectors, including digital technology, renewable energy, transport infrastructure, healthcare, education and research.

articles.title: Human-Elephant conflict: Govt to construct high-tech solar-powered elephant fences
articles.text:
The government is prepared to allocate all necessary funds for the construction of high-quality elephant fences, regardless of the cost, Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government Prof. Chandana Abeyratne has stated.
The Minister said protecting the lives and property of people affected by the human-elephant conflict, while ensuring their ability to engage in farming activities and live without fear, remains a key responsibility of the government.
He made the remarks during a special discussion held at the Anamaduwa Divisional Secretariat on October 14, focusing on long-term solutions to the human-elephant conflict.
According to the Minister, the government plans to construct high-tech solar-powered electric elephant fences, strengthen existing boundaries and establish field control units to prevent elephants from entering residential and agricultural areas.
He revealed that funds have already been allocated for the construction of an initial five-kilometre section of the proposed elephant fence.
The Department of Wildlife Conservation has been instructed to identify the exact boundaries, determine the required length and prepare a comprehensive cost estimate for the project.
The proposed fence, based on the solar-powered electric elephant fence model in Siyambalanduwa, is expected to be constructed along the banks of Mee Oya and the Kurunegala District boundary.
The Minister explained that existing elephant fences in the area are frequently damaged by elephants, despite daily repairs carried out by Civil Defence Force personnel.
Meanwhile, the government is also implementing measures to improve food and water availability within natural elephant habitats to discourage elephants from entering villages.
These measures include removing invasive plants from the Thabbowa Tank Reserve, renovating 11 tanks in the Galawila Park and restoring the Mahasen Tank near Wanathavilluwa.
The Minister further stated that efforts are underway to safely guide elephant herds, particularly those with calves, back to their natural habitats in the Thabbowa and Wilpattu sanctuaries without causing harm.
Preliminary arrangements are also underway to establish a special control unit in Kottukachchiya to coordinate operations related to the human-elephant conflict.
The Minister emphasised that the government’s ultimate objective is to ensure the safety of communities while protecting elephants within their natural habitats.

According to the Minister, the government plans to construct high-tech solar-powered electric elephant fences, strengthen existing boundaries and establish field control units to prevent elephants from entering residential and agricultural areas.

articles.title: Govt paid £24,536 for Yoshitha Rajapaksa’s UK Naval Training, court told
articles.text:
A sum of £24,536 had been paid using government funds for former Navy Lieutenant Yoshitha Rajapaksa, son of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, to attend the ‘Royal Navy Young Officers Course’ at the Royal Navy Training College in Britain, it was reported.
According to the state newspaper Dinamina , the details were revealed during testimony given by a Navy representative on behalf of former Navy Commander Admiral Travis Sinniah before the Colombo High Court on Thursday (15).
The witness stated that former Navy Commander Wasantha Karannagoda had sent a letter to the Secretary of the Ministry of Defence on May 19, 2014, requesting approval for the funds required for Yoshitha Rajapaksa to participate in the training programme.
Responding to questions raised during cross-examination, the witness explained that payments for Navy officers attending overseas training programmes are generally made in foreign currencies, including US dollars and British pounds.
The details were revealed when the money laundering case filed against Yoshitha Rajapaksa was taken up before Colombo High Court Judge Udesh Ranatunga.
Rajapaksa faces charges under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act over his alleged failure to explain the source of nearly Rs. 735 million acquired between August 1, 2012, and August 29, 2013, in Rajagiriya and Bambalapitiya.
The charges also relate to allegations that funds believed to have been obtained through unlawful activities were deposited in bank accounts and fixed deposits.
Meanwhile, Navy Captain Nuwan Thushara Arangala, who testified for the prosecution, revealed that Yoshitha Rajapaksa had received a total of Rs. 5,159,626.37 in salaries and allowances during nine years of service in the Navy.
The court was informed that Rajapaksa had served as a Navy Lieutenant from December 14, 2006, until February 28, 2017, while his service had been suspended on February 28, 2016.
According to the testimony, his monthly gross salary was Rs. 16,390, in addition to allowances for food, uniforms, housing and special duties.
The witness clarified that the stated allowances did not include payments made for overseas training programmes or participation in sporting events while representing the Navy.
During the proceedings, the prosecution also submitted Yoshitha Rajapaksa’s annual declarations of assets and liabilities for the period from 2009 to 2015.
A National Savings Bank official also testified regarding fixed deposit and savings accounts maintained by Rajapaksa, stating that no withdrawals had been made from the accounts since they were opened.
The court further heard testimony concerning the appointment of a guardian for Daisy Forrest, the second defendant in the case, and matters relating to the clearance of an imported Outside Broadcasting (OB) truck associated with the CSN television channel.
Further examination of witnesses was scheduled for October 30, with the court instructing 11 prosecution witnesses to appear on that date.
articles.summary: A sum of £24,536 had been paid using government funds for former Navy Lieutenant Yoshitha Rajapaksa, son of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, to attend the ‘Royal Navy Young Officers Course’ at the Royal Navy Training College in Britain, it was reported.

articles.title: Hambantota Port handles over 167,000 vehicles between March 2025 and September 2026
articles.text:
Hambantota International Port (HIP) delivered a total of 167,569 vehicles during the March–December 2025 period and the first nine months of 2026, according to a statement issued by Hambantota International Port Group (HIPG).
Of the total, 86,389 vehicles were delivered between March and December 2025, including 30,809 brand-new vehicles and 55,580 used vehicles.
A further 81,180 vehicles were delivered between January and September 2026, comprising 25,018 brand-new vehicles and 56,162 used vehicles.
HIPG stated that it had worked closely with the Vehicle Importers’ Association of Lanka (VIAL) to support vehicle importers amid increased demand and disruptions affecting vehicle movements.
The Association, which represents more than 450 members across Sri Lanka, has recognised HIPG’s operational flexibility and support in addressing challenges faced by vehicle importers.
According to HIPG, the Port provided demurrage waivers and concessions during vehicle import restrictions, when customers’ vehicles remained at the Port for extended periods.
More recently, disruptions to vehicle transhipment through the Gulf region prompted HIPG to introduce a storage cap mechanism to help affected importers manage costs.
HIPG Chief Executive Officer Wilson Qu said meeting increased demand required not only handling capacity but also an understanding of customers’ operational needs and the ability to respond to changing conditions.
Meanwhile, HIPG General Manager of Commercial and Marketing Bindu Ranasinghe said the Port’s focus had been on helping customers manage costs while ensuring the efficient movement of cargo.
VIAL President Sampath Merenchige also acknowledged HIPG’s responsiveness and flexibility, stating that its timely operational solutions and cost-management measures had been valuable to the Association’s members.
articles.summary: Hambantota International Port (HIP) delivered a total of 167,569 vehicles during the March–December 2025 period and the first nine months of 2026, according to a statement issued by Hambantota International Port Group (HIPG). Of the total, 86,389 vehicles were delivered between March and December 2025, including 30,809 brand-new vehicles and 55,580 used vehicles.

articles.title: St. Peter’s College Old Boys’ Union Announces Centenary Celebrations Marking 100 Years of Service to the Peterite Community
articles.text:
The St. Peter’s College Old Boys’ Union (OBU) today announced a year-long program of celebrations marking its Centenary: 100 years since the Union’s founding in 1927. The announcement was made at a media briefing at the Patron’s Auditorium, St. Peter’s College OBU Secretariat, attended by members of the media and the OBU’s Centenary Organizing Committee.
The Centenary Year is guided by the theme “Honoring the Past. Strengthening the Present. Inspiring the Peterite of Tomorrow.” Each part of the theme is one of the three pillars on which the year’s celebrations and initiatives are built:
Honoring the Past: paying tribute to the generations of Old Boys whose time, resources, and loyalty have sustained the Union for a century, and to the enduring bond, formed at St. Peter’s College, that connects Peterites across Sri Lanka and around the
Strengthening the Present: investing in the College and its community today through teacher development, infrastructure improvements at the OBU Secretariat, and programs that support current students.
Inspiring the Peterite of Tomorrow: equipping the next generation of students with the skills, opportunities, and support they need to thrive well beyond school, so that the Union’s legacy continues for the next hundred years.
“Reaching a century is a milestone few alumni associations anywhere achieve, and it belongs to every generation of Old Boys who gave their time and loyalty to help this Union grow from strength to strength,” said Dr. Nirmal De Silva, President of the St. Peter’s College Old Boys’ Union . “Honoring that past also means strengthening what we do today and inspiring the Peterites of tomorrow. As we mark our Centenary, we want every Peterite, wherever in the world he may be, to feel the same sense of belonging that has held our family together since 1927.”
Centenary Launch Event: October 18, 2026
The centerpiece of the celebrations will be the Centenary Launch Event on Sunday, October 18, 2026 . All Old Boys are invited to the College for a day of celebration, with the following program:
8:00 m. — Holy Mass
Unveiling of the cover of the Centenary Coffee Table Book
Centenary Breakfast

articles.text:
Businessman Dudley Sirisena has appealed to wildlife authorities to seek additional assistance to save the ailing tusker Kawanthissa, who has been receiving medical treatment over the past few days.
His appeal comes amid growing concerns over the elephant’s condition after it was reportedly spotted lying in a paddy field.
In a social media statement, Sirisena questioned whether the Department of Wildlife Conservation and the veterinary teams currently treating the elephant could manage the situation without additional support.
He urged authorities to identify what assistance was required to save the tusker, offering to provide any help necessary.
Meanwhile, Environment Minister Dammika Patabedige recently conducted an emergency inspection to review Kawanthissa’s condition and the ongoing treatment plan.
The treatment is being coordinated by experts from the Department of Wildlife Conservation, the Department of National Zoological Gardens and the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine at the University of Peradeniya.
The minister has also instructed officials to arrange additional veterinary assistance, deploy thermal drone technology to monitor the elephant’s movements at night and coordinate with the armed forces for possible emergency support.
A 25-member emergency response team and specialized equipment, including lifting gear and heavy machinery, are also being considered in case urgent intervention becomes necessary.
Authorities are continuing daily reviews of the elephant’s condition and treatment plan.

articles.title: At least 5 killed in Houthi attack on Yemen’s presidential palace in Aden
articles.text:
At least five people have been killed in the vicinity of the al-Maashiq presidential palace in Yemen’s port city of Aden after Houthi missile strikes.
The Yemeni health minister says five people were killed and 16 others injured in the Houthi missile attack that targeted the al-Maashiq Presidential Palace in Yemen’s Aden on Thursday.
The Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said in a social media post on Thursday that Houthis had targeted the al-Maashiq presidential palace with five missiles.
The government says the prime minister and other officials are safe, but two of his bodyguards were killed in the attack.
Plumes of smoke could be seen rising from the vicinity of the palace.
Al Jazeera correspondents reported earlier on Thursday that there were explosions near the palace.
The palace is considered the headquarters and the seat of power for the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government.
Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry, reporting from the Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa, said the attacks on the headquarters of the internationally recognised government are the “first of their kind” by the Houthis.
“This is an indication that the escalation is going to intensify between both sides,” Mawry said, adding that fears are now growing inside the country of “an all-out civil war” that could potentially drag in other regional powers besides Saudi Arabia.
The attack in Aden came as fighting between the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), and Saudi-backed forces intensified in Taiz, which is effectively under siege by the Houthis.
Controlling Taiz, Yemen’s third city and the broader Taiz governorate, in the southwest of the country would ensure control over the critical Bab al-Mandeb strait for either side.
Forces allied with the Yemeni government said they are repelling a Houthi attack on Dhubab airport.
The pro-government Homeland Shield Force said in a statement that they are, along with the Southern Giants Brigades, securing the airport in the coastal city of Dhubab in Taiz governorate.
Aid agencies say the escalating violence in Taiz is pushing the healthcare system towards breaking point.
On Sunday, the Ministry of Public Health warned of a “humanitarian catastrophe” there.
Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition says Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport has come under at least 20 Houthi attacks over the past 11 days with dozens of other airports, oil facilities and ports also targeted.
Major-General Turki al-Maliki, the spokesperson for the alliance, released footage showing strikes on the main airport with passengers seen fleeing for safety, during a news conference in the Saudi capital.
The coalition says the Houthi attacks have killed 17 people and injured more than 300.
Al-Maliki also accused the Houthis of obtaining ballistic missiles from other countries in the region.
Mohamad Elmasry, a professor at the Doha Institute for Graduate Studies, said the Saudi-led coalition’s news conference was intended as a response “to some of the, perhaps, military and security failures”.
“There’s kind of an image problem there because this is maybe affecting the perception of Saudi deterrence, the fact that missiles are getting through,” he told Al Jazeera.
Elmasry said the Houthis also have an image crisis, with the global community viewing their actions as “reprehensible, in particular these targeting civilian infrastructure”. (Al Jazeera)
articles.summary: At least five people have been killed in the vicinity of the al-Maashiq presidential palace in Yemen’s port city of Aden after Houthi missile strikes. The Yemeni health minister says five people were killed and 16 others injured in the Houthi missile attack that targeted the al-Maashiq Presidential Palace in Yemen’s Aden on Thursday.

She further stated that the President respects the judiciary, the country’s culture and the Constitution, adding that these principles have guided his previous decisions and would continue to guide his future actions.
The Prime Minister made the statement in response to questions concerning a protest march launched by Buddhist monks from Kandy, initially opposing the requirement for Gnanasara Thera to wear prison attire, which has since shifted towards demanding a presidential pardon.

articles.title: SAWM SL kicks off groundbreaking AI training for journalists, civil society & Govt representatives
articles.text:
South Asian Women in Media (SAWM) -Sri Lanka launched its latest training series, Digital Equity SL –Responsible AI Empowering Women, Media & Civil Society, to strengthen AI literacy among multiple sectors in Sri Lanka at the Mandarina Hotel in Colombo on Tuesday 13th October 2026, with the High Commissioner for Canada in Sri Lanka Isabelle Martin as the Guest of Honour.
Supported by the Canada Fund for Local Initiatives (CFLI), the initiative equips Sri Lankan journalists, policy professionals, and civil society leaders with essential tools to navigate artificial intelligence, reduce algorithmic bias, and use data-driven strategies responsibly.
In her opening remarks, the High Commissioner said “I encourage all participants here today to be part of the effort, and to help ensure that technology strengthens, rather than undermines, equality, rights, and freedom of expression. You also have a vital role to play in helping the public understand these technologies, challenging disinformation, exposing digital harms, and ensuring that conversations about AI remain grounded in people, rights, dignity, and democracy.”
As generative AI and automated decision-making systems rapidly reshape public discourse, information ecosystems, and public policy, this hands-on workshop series addresses the urgent need for inclusive digital literacy and gender-sensitive tech governance.
The interactive curriculum covers a range of topics including factchecking AI-generated content, deepfake detection, algorithmic accountability, frameworks for inclusive tech governance, data privacy regulation, leveraging AI tools for advocacy, monitoring digital human rights violations, and countering technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV). The training series is being delivered by Dr. Sanjana Hattotuwa, an authority on digital safety, disinformation, and social media.
“Artificial intelligence holds immense potential for Sri Lanka, but without intentional intervention, it risks compounding existing inequalities and spreading misinformation,” said Sharmini Boyle, program lead and trustee, SAWM Sri Lanka. Trustee Hana Ibrahim added that “by bringing journalists, policy advocates, and civil society together into the same training space, we are building a collaborative ecosystem that holds technology accountable while using it to elevate underrepresented voices.”
Designed to train over 120 participants, four other training programs will be conducted on October 20 (Jaffna), October 27 (Kandy), November 3 (Puttalam) and November 10 (Colombo). Each location zeroes in on specialized priorities—from Tamil-language AI models in Jaffna to multi-sector governance in Colombo—ensuring participants leave with actionable prompt toolkits, deepfake detection workflows, and strategies to counter technology-facilitated gender-based violence. The training workshops are being organised in collaboration with the Sri Lanka Working Journalists’ Association, Sri Lanka Muslim Media Forum and the Jaffna Press Club.
South Asian Women in Media (SAWM) -Sri Lanka is part of a regional network of women working in print, broadcast, and digital media across South Asia. SAWM is dedicated to advocating for media freedom, gender equity in workplaces, and building capacity through professional development and safety initiatives.

articles.title: Tesla’s new Roadster makes a flying debut, hitting 60 MPH in under a second
articles.text:
Tesla unveiled its long-anticipated Roadster on Thursday during a dramatic event in which the vehicle used compressed-air thrusters to fly off a ramp and perform a midair maneuver.
The vehicle was seen flying, performing a midair flip and accelerating from zero to 60 mph in under a second.
“Turns out the future does have flying cars,” Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas.
Vice President of Vehicle Engineering Lars Moravy added, “Flying cars are real.”
The jaw-dropping showcase featured the new Roadster accelerating up a massive curved ramp and using a fan-based suction system to remain attached until it was completely upside down before using integrated cold-gas thrusters developed in collaboration with SpaceX to launch off the ramp, flip in midair and land safely back on the ground.
In another demonstration, the Roadster launched over a lineup of cars and a semi-truck, performing a midair flip before landing safely on the other side.
Musk said certain versions of the Roadster can accelerate from zero to 60 mph in less than one second and reach a top speed of more than 230 mph. During the event, Tesla demonstrated a Roadster accelerating to 60 mph in under a second.
“Every car on the road today is limited by one thing: tire grip Roadster’s thruster system generates 4–5x the force the tires can. More force on the same mass means significantly better acceleration – physics does the rest,” Tesla said on X.
Nearly a decade after the Roadster’s initial 2017 concept debut, the vehicle left audiences in awe with the gravity-defying demonstration that deployed SpaceX’s rocket technology.
“Today, Roadster presents a new moment in history – the best of the last human-driven cars,” Tesla wrote on X.
Tesla executives announced at Thursday’s event that production would begin in 2028.
Musk and other Tesla executives did ​not outline the cost at Thursday’s event, but nearly a decade ago the company quoted a base price of $200,000.
Tesla’s reservation page for the Roadster after Thursday’s event listed a $50,000 reservation payment for the “Performance” version and a $250,000 reservation payment for the “Thrust” version, which features “acceleration thrusters.” An invite-only “Rocket” variant is a single-seat model with a “full flight ​system.”
When Tesla revealed a prototype of the car in 2017, it said that deliveries would begin in 2020. (Fox Business)

articles.title: US teen held over Hindu temple attack plot
articles.text:
A 19-year-old American who expressed ⁠white supremacist ⁠views has been arrested on the day United States police believe he tried to attack a Hindu place of worship.
Police in the state of Illinois say they have thwarted a potential mass shooting and arrested Alexandros Paporakis, a Taco Bell cashier from the Chicago suburb of Palatine.
Prosecutors say he told colleagues he “couldn’t wait” to kill Indian people.
The case comes amid mounting concern among Indian Americans about hostility towards their community, fuelled by bitter political fights over immigration and skilled-worker visas.
So what do we know about the alleged plot, and is anti-Indian racism really on the rise in the US?
What happened?
Investigators say they believe Paporakis planned to attack the largest Hindu temple in Aurora, about 40 miles (65km) southwest of the Chicago suburb of Palatine in Illinois.
“However, the specific intended location has not been confirmed and remains under investigation,” police said.
Paporakis allegedly told colleagues that Sunday would be “a special day”.
According to prosecutors, a work colleague told investigators that Paporakis telephoned him on Sunday afternoon, saying his gun had jammed, ABC7 Chicago reported. He allegedly told his coworker he had left “super fast” without being seen.
He allegedly sent a video of the rifle failing to fire and said he wanted to try again once it was repaired, Fox 32 Chicago reported.
Two co-workers called police. Officers from Palatine and neighbouring Mount Prospect then arrested him as he left his home.
“The seriousness of this alleged threat cannot be overstated,” said Palatine Police Chief William Nord.
Paporakis faces felony charges of “making a terrorist threat” and “unlawful possession of a weapon”.
On Wednesday, a judge ordered him to be held in jail before a trial.
What more do we know about the suspect?
Prosecutors say Paporakis openly described himself to colleagues at work as a white supremacist.
He allegedly sent a co-worker an eight-page document titled, Why I fought: A.K.A. (Aurora Shooter’s Manifesto), according to a court document obtained by The Associated Press news agency.
It described Indian, Jewish and Black people as “subhumans” and set out a plan to kill as many of them as possible.
In it, he allegedly referred to himself as “a sociopathic white supremacist Neo Nazi filled with hatred, fantasising about mass murder nearly every day”.
According to prosecutors, he wrote that he had been planning the attack for two years and had researched his target using YouTube and Google Street View, Fox 32 reported.
Prosecutors also said he had mental health issues and lived with his mother, according to ABC7.
A search of his home turned up an AR-style rifle without a serial number, loaded magazines, a gas canister labelled with a slur aimed at South Asians and items bearing Nazi symbolism. (Al Jazeera)

Investigators say they believe Paporakis planned to attack the largest Hindu temple in Aurora, about 40 miles (65km) southwest of the Chicago suburb of Palatine in Illinois.

articles.title: Police freeze Rs. 85 million in property & cash in Jaffna
articles.text:
The Illegal Assets Investigation Division of the Sri Lanka Police has issued freezing orders on cash and property worth approximately Rs. 85 million, suspected to have been acquired through drug trafficking.
According to police, the assets include a two-story house valued at more than Rs. 70 million in Jaffna, and Rs. 15 million in cash.
The investigation stems from the arrest of five suspects by Special Task Force (STF) officers in Jaffna on August 31, 2023, after they were found in possession of Rs. 15 million in cash. A lorry was also seized during the operation.
Further investigations revealed that one of the suspects, a 32-year-old resident of Mathagal, had allegedly used proceeds from drug trafficking to construct the two-story house.
Police said the Rs. 15 million seized during the initial arrests remains in the custody of the Jaffna court.
Accordingly, the Illegal Assets Investigation Division issued freezing orders on the house and cash under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, effective October 15, 2026, for a period of 14 days.
Further investigations are underway.

articles.title: Justice Minister responds to UNP statement on Gnanasara Thera case
articles.text:
Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara issued a written response today (15) addressing a statement released by the United National Party (UNP) regarding the imprisonment of Venerable Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera.
The UNP issued its statement yesterday (14), citing comments made by Joint Opposition Convener Professor G.L. Peiris. The party argued that the Prisons Department Standing Orders already contain clear provisions governing the attire required when escorting imprisoned monks and religious leaders outside. The UNP claimed that appointing a committee to present recommendations on the matter was a “dishonest” effort to cover up and prolong the issue, adding that the government should apologize to the Mahanayake Thera and the Sangha Sabha of the Kotte Sri Kalyani Samagri Dharma Maha Sangha Sabha of the Siam Maha Nikaya over the removal of Gnanasara Thera’s robes.
In his reply, the Justice Minister stated that the UNP “intentionally”quoted only a single portion of Prisons Standing Order No. 550 to present a “distorted” view that “misleads” the public. Nanayakkara noted that it is deeply regrettable for a responsible political party to circulate distorted views on a socially sensitive matter involving an imprisoned Buddhist monk.
He highlighted that anyone with even a minimal understanding of the law should know that presenting facts based on only a fraction of a legal provision leads to an incorrect or incomplete understanding. The Minister added that the UNP’s media release created a “misleading” impression by failing to present the full text of the relevant Standing Order and ignoring the specific duration of the prison sentence handed to Gnanasara Thera.
articles.summary: Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara issued a written response today (15) addressing a statement released by the United National Party (UNP) regarding the imprisonment of Venerable Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera.

articles.title: Fake SriLankan Airlines app used to steal bank details in
articles.text:
The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has informed the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court of a large-scale financial scam involving a fraudulent mobile application designed to resemble the official SriLankan Airlines app.
The CID told Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama that fraudsters had used the airline’s branding and logo to promote a fake application offering a 50% return on airline ticket purchases.
According to investigators, users were initially charged Rs. 250 to register on the application.
Once registered, users were allegedly encouraged to enter personal information, which was then stolen and used to gain unauthorized access to their bank accounts.
The CID’s Computer Crime Investigation Division told the court that the fraudulent application had allegedly been used to steal millions of rupees from unsuspecting customers.
Investigators also revealed that victims were often unaware their banking details had been compromised, with some noticing only that their mobile phones were overheating and their battery life was gradually declining.
The CID said several Sri Lankans who allegedly sold access to their bank accounts to facilitate the fraudulent transactions had already been arrested.
Further investigations are underway to identify and arrest those responsible for operating the fake application.

articles.title: Environment Minister inspects ailing elephant Kavantissa
articles.text:
Minister of Environment Dr. Dammika Patabedige conducted an emergency inspection visit to review the current health condition of the ailing elephant “Kavantissa” and formalize ongoing medical treatment protocols.
During the visit, the Minister focused on the elephant’s health status and the treatment plan jointly formulated by experts from the Department of Wildlife Conservation, the Department of National Zoological Gardens and professors from the Peradeniya Faculty of Veterinary Medicine. He instructed officials to secure additional expert veterinary assistance from the zoological department as needed and to strengthen inter-agency coordination.
To monitor the elephant’s night-time behavior, movement patterns, drinking habits and other activities, the Minister intervened to coordinate the procurement of thermal drone technology. This equipment will provide clearer nocturnal activity data to assist the veterinary team in making informed treatment decisions.
Emphasizing the need for a rapid response plan in case of sudden health changes, the Minister instructed relevant sectors to coordinate with the Sri Lanka Armed Forces. This includes the potential deployment of a 25-member emergency support team, alongside pre-arranging specialized equipment, safety harnesses, lifting gear, transport assistance, backhoes, boom trucks or other suitable machinery for urgent medical positioning.
Daily updates and progress reviews regarding treatment plans and logistical needs will continue to be coordinated through daily Zoom discussions involving veterinary surgeons and officials. The Minister stressed that while aiming for the best possible recovery outcomes, authorities should remain fully prepared for any severe contingencies to protect the elephant’s life and health under expert medical guidance.

articles.title: School roof collapse in Pakistan kills at least 29 people

At least 28 students and a teacher were killed and more than 50 others injured, when the roof of a private school collapsed today (15) morning in Peshawar, the capital of Pakistan’s northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, authorities stated.
A spokesperson for Lady Reading Hospital, Mohammad Asim confirmed the casualties and stated that some of the wounded remain in critical condition. All the children killed or injured were age 13 or younger, he noted. The hospital has declared an emergency as medical staff treat the wounded.
Reports state that the school had approximately 350 registered students, adding that casualties could rise as dozens of the wounded remain hospitalized in serious condition. Authorities have ordered an official investigation to determine the exact cause of the collapse.
Reacting to the tragedy, Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar shared a statement on X, “Our children are our most precious asset, and every such loss is a tragedy for the entire country. My heartfelt condolences and prayers are with the bereaved families.”
He added, “The prime minister and the government have taken serious note of the situation. Ensuring the safety and protection of our children must remain paramount.”

articles.title: Lanka Sathosa recorded Rs. 22,000 million loss by end-2024: Trade Minister
articles.text:
Minister of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development Wasantha Samarasinghe said that Lanka Sathosa accumulated a total loss of Rs. 22,000 million by the end of 2024.
“When we took over in 2024, at the end of 2024, the loss of Lanka Sathosa was Rs. 22,000 million,” the Minister stated, detailing the government’s intervention to address short term debt obligations. “Our government came and zeroed the Rs. 5,300 million overdraft that existed. Lanka Sathosa was paying Rs.30 to 40 million a month in interest Rs. 480 million a year. That means the loss was increasing further.” he added.
The minister further explained “The loss of 22,000 million as of December 2024 was tied to payments owed to suppliers, not a small amount, Rs. 14,000 million. So, we are reducing the payments owed to suppliers, reducing loss making operations, freeing up the burden and talking about rebuilding Sathosa,”
He also said, “When Ravi Karunanayake was asked this question, he gave an answer about Lanka Sathosa, asking why it shouldn’t be given away or sold. That is what they said. But as a government, Lanka Sathosa is built as an institution that fulfills a responsible role in the goods distribution process,”
Samarasinghe emphasized that Lanka Sathosa must not be viewed merely as a state venture, but as a key market mechanism. “This is not just a state institution; this is the mechanism we have to use, along with the private sector, to control goods prices,” he added.

articles.title: Ella eatery fined Rs. 260,000 for overpricing water bottles, displaying expired sodas
articles.text:
The Bandarawela Magistrate’s Court has ordered a fine of Rs. 260,000 against an eatery in Ella following a Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) prosecution for overpricing bottled water and displaying expired beverages for sale.
The legal action was brought against the particular eatery after Badulla District investigation officers uncovered multiple violations during a raid conducted on October 2, 2026.
Inspectors found that the establishment was selling 1,000 ml (1-litre) bottled drinking water for Rs. 200, exceeding the mandated Maximum Retail Price (MRP) of Rs. 120 by Rs. 80 per bottle.
The CAA emphasized that the legal MRP remains unchanged regardless of venue or whether the buyer is a domestic or international tourist. Additionally, the inspection revealed six 400 ml soda bottles that had expired on September 29, 2026, displayed among other inventory for sale.
The CAA noted that merely displaying expired food and beverage items constitutes a legal offense, posing potential public health risks and undermining consumer trust.
When the case was called before the Bandarawela Magistrate’s Court on October 14, 2026, the defendant entered a guilty plea to all charges, resulting in the Rs. 260,000 fine.
Authorities stressed that operating costs do not justify exceeding price controlled limits. Furthermore, officials highlighted that poor experiences in key tourist hubs like Ella can damage both individual establishment reputations and the broader standing of Sri Lanka’s tourism sector.
The CAA continues its islandwide enforcement drives and urges the public to report pricing violations and expired stock through its 1977 consumer hotline during office hours.

articles.title: Deputy Minister seeks correction over alleged AI-generated image shown on TV
articles.text:
Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Chathuranga Abeysinghe has sought a formal clarification and correction from a private television channel over the alleged use of an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated photograph concerning him during a television discussion programme.
An official letter dated October 15 has been sent to the television channel, requesting an investigation into the authenticity of the photograph displayed by former Minister Wimal Weerawansa during the programme.
According to a statement issued by the Deputy Minister’s Office, the photograph displayed and discussed by Weerawansa was not an original selfie taken by Abeysinghe but an image allegedly manipulated using AI technology.
The letter warns that presenting an artificially generated image as an authentic photograph could mislead the public and damage an individual’s reputation.
It further raises concerns that the use of such images during discussions involving sensitive ethnic and religious matters could create misunderstandings and potentially fuel racial or religious tensions.
The Deputy Minister’s Office has also questioned whether the programme’s presenter took adequate steps to verify the authenticity and source of the photograph before allowing it to be discussed on air.
Accordingly, the letter requests the television channel to verify the photograph’s authenticity and source, make necessary corrections to the relevant video, issue a clear public correction through the same programme and provide a written explanation of the action taken.
The statement emphasised that the request was not intended to restrict political expression but to ensure accuracy and responsible media practices.
The latest development follows allegations raised by Deputy Minister Abeysinghe against former Minister Wimal Weerawansa over the use of the photograph during the television discussion.
In an earlier social media post, Abeysinghe shared what he described as the original photograph alongside the allegedly AI-manipulated version.
He claimed that the original photograph showed him with an individual identified as Amal, who had helped protect protesters during an attack by Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) supporters during the 2022 Aragalaya protest movement.
According to Abeysinghe, Amal was among a small group of individuals who initially confronted the attackers, and the photograph had been taken in recognition of his actions.
However, the Deputy Minister alleged that the original image had subsequently been manipulated using AI technology to portray Amal as a Buddhist monk.
Abeysinghe criticised Weerawansa for allegedly relying on the manipulated image to make political claims during the television programme.
The Deputy Minister’s Office has called on the television channel to take prompt and responsible action to correct any misleading information and safeguard public trust in the media.
articles.summary: Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Chathuranga Abeysinghe has sought a formal clarification and correction from a private television channel over the alleged use of an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated photograph concerning him during a television discussion programme.

articles.title: Construction begins on new Coastal Park in Mannar
articles.text:
Construction work on a new coastal recreational park in the Silavathurai–Arippu area of Mannar has commenced, with the project aimed at protecting the coastline, supporting the local fishing community and promoting tourism.
The foundation stone for the project was laid yesterday (14) under the patronage of Deputy Minister of Environment Anton Jayakody.
According to the Ministry of Environment, the project is being implemented as part of the Government’s coastal conservation programme, which includes the development of recreational parks in coastal areas across the country.
The Silavathurai–Arippu coastal park project was initiated considering the tourism potential of the area surrounding the historic Doric Bungalow in Mannar.
The project aims to address severe coastal erosion along the Silavathurai–Arippu coastline while protecting the surrounding coastal environment.
It will also improve facilities and provide additional space for local fishermen to moor their boats, supporting fishing activities in the area.
The Ministry noted that several similar coastal recreational park projects across the island are currently nearing completion.
The coastal conservation activities in the Silavathurai–Arippu area are being carried out jointly by the Ministry of Environment and the Department of Coast Conservation and Coastal Resource Management, using a scientific approach to coastal protection.
articles.summary: Construction work on a new coastal recreational park in the Silavathurai–Arippu area of Mannar has commenced, with the project aimed at protecting the coastline, supporting the local fishing community and promoting tourism. The Silavathurai–Arippu coastal park project was initiated considering the tourism potential of the area surrounding the historic Doric Bungalow in Mannar.

articles.title: Sri Lanka receives Rs. 330 Mn worth of cancer medicines from US charity
articles.text:
Sri Lanka has received a donation of essential cancer medicines worth Rs. 330 million from a US-based charitable organisation, while an agreement has also been signed to provide 600 specialised wheelchairs for patients with spinal cord injuries.
The donation was made by Latter-day Saint Charities (LDSC), affiliated with The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, to the Ministry of Health and Mass Media on Wednesday (14).
According to the Ministry, the donated medicines include several essential oncology drugs, such as Oxaliplatin 100mg injections, Abiraterone 250mg tablets and Methotrexate 500mg/5ml injections, intended for the treatment of cancer patients in Sri Lanka.
The medicines were officially handed over to Ministry Secretary Dr. Anil Jasinghe by LDSC Asia Area Director Lui Wing Chung Mickey and Asia Area Manager Apapohn Pinsakol Saengsin at the Ministry premises.
During the event, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was also signed between the Ministry and the US-based organisation for the donation of 600 specialised wheelchairs to rehabilitation hospitals and centres treating patients with spinal cord injuries.
The wheelchair donation marks the second phase of the organisation’s humanitarian assistance programme in Sri Lanka.
Under the first phase in 2023, LDSC donated 570 wheelchairs, which have since been distributed to patients through rehabilitation centres across the country.
The latest programme will also include specialised training for healthcare personnel on wheelchair prescription, use and repairs, in accordance with World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines.
Doctors, physiotherapists, occupational therapists and wheelchair workshop staff are expected to receive training under the initiative.
Meanwhile, the Ministry noted that LDSC had also donated essential cancer medicines worth approximately US$ 2 million (Rs. 660 million) to Sri Lanka over the past two years.
In recognition of the latest donation, a special Certificate of Appreciation arranged by Minister of Health Nalinda Jayatissa was presented to the organisation’s Asia Area Director by Ministry Secretary Dr. Anil Jasinghe.

articles.title: New website launched for public inquiries on education reforms
articles.text:
The Government has launched a new official website to provide accurate information and address public inquiries regarding Sri Lanka’s proposed education reforms.
The Reform Information & Enquiry Service (RIES) website, https://edureformfact.moe.gov.lk , was officially launched with the participation of Prime Minister and Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Harini Amarasuriya.
The launch took place during a programme held at Temple Trees yesterday (14), attended by heads of electronic and print media institutions to discuss the implementation of the new education reforms.
The website has been developed to communicate accurate information about the reforms and allow members of the public to submit questions regarding the proposed changes to the education system.
Addressing the gathering, Prime Minister Amarasuriya emphasised that the reforms represent a transformation of the entire education system rather than merely a revision of the school curriculum.
“This is a transformation of the entire education system that goes beyond a change in the curriculum. The future of our country is built on quality education,” she stated.
The Prime Minister noted that the first phase of the reforms commenced with Grade 1 in 2026, while plans are underway to introduce the reforms to Grade 6 in 2027.
She said teacher training, infrastructure development and digitalisation initiatives are already being implemented to ensure the education system is prepared for the changes.
Highlighting the role of the media, the Prime Minister stressed the importance of creating a national dialogue on education reforms and ensuring that accurate information reaches the public.
“We may have different political ideologies, but it is important that we do not use children’s education as a political battleground,” she said.
Meanwhile, Professor Prabhath Jayasinghe, Co-Chairperson of the Subcommittee on Public Awareness of Education Reforms, explained that the proposed changes aim to move away from teacher-centred, memorisation-based education towards student-centred learning connected to real-world experiences.
He said the reforms would also introduce continuous assessment methods to evaluate students’ analytical, creative and problem-solving abilities, rather than relying primarily on final examinations.
The programme concluded with a discussion among media representatives, senior journalists and education experts on the proposed changes to Sri Lanka’s education system.
articles.summary: The Government has launched a new official website to provide accurate information and address public inquiries regarding Sri Lanka’s proposed education reforms. The Reform Information & Enquiry Service (RIES) website, https://edureformfact.moe.gov.lk , was officially launched with the participation of Prime Minister and Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Harini Amarasuriya.

articles.title: Dehiwala Zoo Zebra recovering well after successful emergency surgery
articles.text:
A zebra at the Dehiwala National Zoological Gardens is recovering well and has resumed eating normally following a successful emergency surgery to remove an obstruction from its digestive tract.
The Department of National Zoological Gardens, providing an update on the animal’s condition, confirmed that the zebra is making a rapid recovery under veterinary care.
According to the Department, the zebra had been showing signs of illness since September 29, prompting veterinary officers to conduct laboratory tests and a scan.
The examinations revealed an obstruction in the animal’s digestive tract, requiring urgent surgical intervention.
Accordingly, a special emergency surgery was performed on October 9, with the participation of veterinary officers and staff of the Department of National Zoological Gardens.
The procedure was conducted under the guidance and participation of Dr. Dammika Perera, Senior Lecturer at the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine of the University of Peradeniya, who specialises in equine species.
The surgery continued for several hours until the early hours of the following morning, during which veterinary surgeons successfully removed a mass of undigested food that had caused the obstruction.
Following the procedure, the zebra was kept under close veterinary supervision for several days.
The Department has now confirmed that the animal is recovering well and has resumed its usual feeding habits.
The Department of National Zoological Gardens also expressed appreciation to Dr. Dammika Perera, veterinary surgeon Dr. Hasitha Rupathunga, the Dehiwala Zoo Veterinary Hospital staff and animal care teams for their contributions to the successful surgery and the zebra’s recovery.

articles.title: Monk who linked assault to NPP now says he assumed victim was protest supporter
articles.text:
Ven. Thiththagalle Anandasiri Thera has responded to allegations by Sri Lanka Police that he spread false information about an assault during a protest march demanding the release of imprisoned Buddhist monk Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, acknowledging that he had initially assumed the injured man was a supporter of the march.
In his initial video, the monk alleged that individuals linked to the ruling National People’s Power (NPP) were responsible for attacking a man who had assisted the protest march from Kandy to Colombo.
However, responding to a police statement rejecting those claims, the monk said he had believed the injured man was someone supporting the march because the assault occurred in front of the protesters.
He did not repeat his earlier allegation directly linking the attackers to the NPP in his latest explanation, instead focusing on the police response to the incident.
The monk maintained that the assault had occurred in the presence of police officers deployed along the protest route and questioned why they had allegedly failed to intervene.
According to Ven. Anandasiri Thera, the victim was bleeding following the attack, and he helped clean the man’s wounds before arranging for him to be taken to hospital by ambulance.
He also claimed that those accompanying the march had recorded the registration number of the motorcycle involved and provided the information to police.
The monk questioned why police had focused on accusing him of spreading misinformation rather than examining the alleged failure of officers to act when the assault occurred.
He further suggested that police had taken action only after his video attracted public attention.
His response follows a statement issued by Sri Lanka Police on Oct. 15, rejecting claims that a supporter of the march had been attacked.
Police said investigations revealed that the incident occurred on Oct. 14 near the Veediyawatta Devalaya in the Weeragula police area following a traffic-related dispute between a man travelling in a lorry and a motorcyclist.
According to police, an argument arising from traffic congestion escalated into a confrontation during which the lorry occupant was struck with a helmet.
Police said the injured man had confirmed in a statement that he was travelling for personal reasons and had no connection to the protest march.
The injured man was admitted to Wathupitiwala Hospital, while the motorcyclist involved in the dispute was also admitted to Gampaha Hospital for treatment.
Police accused Ven. Anandasiri Thera of misleading the public by presenting the injured man as a supporter of the march who had been deliberately attacked.
The monk, however, rejected suggestions that he had deliberately spread false information, maintaining that he had intervened to help an injured person and publicised the incident to draw attention to the assault.
He also criticised the government’s handling of the protest and reiterated that the march would continue towards Colombo despite heavy rain.
Police said the matter would be reported to court and warned that legal action could be taken against those spreading false or unverified information capable of causing public unrest.
Further investigations are underway.
articles.summary: Ven. Thiththagalle Anandasiri Thera has responded to allegations by Sri Lanka Police that he spread false information about an assault during a protest march demanding the release of imprisoned Buddhist monk Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, acknowledging that he had initially assumed the injured man was a supporter of the march.
